suhoor.name: Middle Eastern Power Bowl
suhoor.description: Ful medames with eggs, tahini, fresh vegetables, and warm pita
suhoor.benefits: High protein and fiber for sustained energy throughout the fast
suhoor.tips: Add a drizzle of olive oil for healthy fats
suhoor.significance: Ful medames has been a staple suhoor in Egypt and the Levant for centuries, providing lasting energy for the long fast.
steps: If using dried fava beans, soak overnight (8–12 hr), then simmer 45–60 min until tender; or use canned, drained fava beans (no cook).
Warm the beans in a pan with a little olive oil and cumin over medium heat for 3–4 min. Mash lightly with a fork.
Fry or poach eggs to your liking (about 2–3 min for fried, 3–4 min for poached).
Slice tomatoes and cucumber (1 min). Warm pita in a dry pan or toaster for 1–2 min.
Serve beans in a bowl, top with tahini, egg, vegetables, and a drizzle of olive oil. Serve with pita.

suhoor.name: South Asian Paratha Breakfast
suhoor.description: Whole wheat paratha with egg curry and lassi
suhoor.benefits: Complex carbohydrates and protein keep you full longer
steps: Make paratha dough: mix 2 cups whole wheat flour with 1 tsp salt and about 3/4 cup water to form a soft dough. Knead 5 min until smooth, cover with a damp cloth, rest 15 min.

Divide dough into 4–6 balls. Roll each into a 6-inch circle, brush with 1 tsp oil or ghee, fold in half twice to make a triangle, then roll out again to 6 inches. Cook on a hot tawa or cast-iron skillet over medium heat 2–3 min per side until golden spots appear and puffed. Keep warm in a towel.

For egg curry: heat 2 tbsp oil, sauté 1 large sliced onion 5–6 min until golden. Add 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp coriander, pinch chili; fry 1 min. Add 2 chopped tomatoes; cook 4–5 min until soft. Add 2 tbsp water, crack in 4 eggs and scramble 2–3 min until set. Season with salt.
For lassi: blend 1 cup yogurt with 1/2 cup cold water, pinch salt or 1 tsp sugar, and 1/4 tsp roasted cumin (1 min). Pour into glasses. Serve parathas with egg curry and lassi.

suhoor.name: Turkish Sahur Spread
suhoor.description: Cheese, olives, eggs, fresh bread, and Turkish tea
suhoor.benefits: Balanced meal with proteins, healthy fats, and carbohydrates
suhoor.tips: Limit caffeine intake; opt for herbal tea if possible
steps: Slice 100–150g feta and arrange on a plate with 1/2 cup olives (black or green). Slice 1–2 tomatoes and 1 cucumber into wedges if using (about 2 min).
Fry or scramble 2–3 eggs to your liking 2–3 min; season with a little salt and black pepper. Keep warm.
Warm or toast 2–3 pieces fresh bread (simit, pide, or baguette) 1–2 min per side. Place honey in a small dish for dipping.

Brew Turkish tea (çay) in a double teapot: boil water in lower pot, add tea to upper pot, steep 5–7 min. Or use caffeine-free herbal tea (e.g. apple, rosehip). Serve everything together for a quick, balanced sahur.

suhoor.name: Indonesian Bubur Ayam
suhoor.description: Savory chicken rice porridge with toppings
suhoor.tips: Prepare the night before for easy morning reheating
steps: Rinse 1 cup rice (1 min) and put in a large pot with 8–10 cups water (or chicken broth). Bring to a boil (about 5 min), then reduce heat and simmer, stirring every 10 min, until rice breaks down into a thick porridge (about 45 min total). Add more water if needed.
Meanwhile, poach or boil chicken breast or thigh 15–20 min until cooked; shred the meat. Save the broth to add to the porridge.
Season the porridge with grated ginger, salt, white pepper, and a little garlic. Add shredded chicken; heat through 2–3 min.
Serve in bowls topped with fried shallots, sliced scallions, soy sauce, and optional soft-boiled egg (6–7 min) and cakwe (fried dough). Add kecap manis and sambal if you like.

suhoor.name: Overnight Oats with Dates
suhoor.description: Steel-cut oats soaked overnight with dates, nuts, and honey
suhoor.benefits: Slow-release energy, easy to digest, no morning cooking needed
suhoor.tips: Add chia seeds for extra fiber and omega-3s
suhoor.significance: Dates and oats align with the Sunnah of breaking fast with dates while providing sustained energy.
steps: In a jar or bowl, combine 1 cup rolled or steel-cut oats, 1 cup milk (or plant-based), 1/4 tsp cinnamon, and 1 tbsp honey. Stir well (1 min).
Chop 2–3 Medjool dates and add to the mixture. Add 2 tbsp almonds (whole or sliced) and optional 1 tbsp chia seeds (1 min).
Cover and refrigerate overnight (at least 4–8 hours). Oats will soften and absorb the liquid.
In the morning, stir and eat cold or microwave 1–2 min. Add extra dates, nuts, or a splash of milk on top if you like.

suhoor.name: Lebanese Man'oushe with Labneh
suhoor.description: Flatbread with za'atar or cheese, served with labneh and olives
suhoor.totalTime: 27 min (+ 30 min rise if making dough)
suhoor.benefits: Filling and hydrating; olive oil and labneh provide sustained energy
suhoor.tips: Man'oushe is a classic Lebanese suhoor; pair with jallab or water
steps: Use store-bought pizza dough or make a simple dough: 2 cups flour, 1 tsp yeast, 1 tsp salt, warm water (5 min). Let rise 30 min.
Preheat oven to 450°F (230°C) (about 10 min). Divide dough into 4–6 rounds and stretch into ovals. Place on a baking sheet (2 min).
Brush each round with olive oil and spread a generous layer of za'atar (thyme, sumac, sesame, salt). Optionally add cheese (akawi or mozzarella) (2 min).
Bake 8–12 min until edges are golden. Serve warm with labneh, olives, sliced tomatoes, and a drizzle of olive oil.

suhoor.name: Jordanian Labneh & Za'atar
suhoor.description: Thick strained yogurt with za'atar, olive oil, and warm bread
suhoor.benefits: Protein-rich and easy to digest; olive oil for lasting energy
suhoor.tips: Traditional Jordanian suhoor; add dates for quick energy
steps: Scoop labneh (strained yogurt) into a shallow bowl. Swirl the top with a spoon and drizzle generously with olive oil (1 min).
Sprinkle za'atar over the labneh. Add a few olives and a pinch of salt if the labneh is plain (1 min).
Warm pita or shrak (thin flatbread) in the oven or on a stove burner 1–2 min until soft. Tear and use to scoop labneh.
Optional: serve with sliced cucumber, tomatoes, and dates for a complete suhoor.

suhoor.name: Nigerian Kunu & Masa
suhoor.benefits: Hydrating and filling; masa is light and easy before dawn
suhoor.tips: Kunu is a traditional Hausa suhoor drink; often served cold
steps: Kunu: Soak millet (or sorghum) overnight. Drain, blend with fresh ginger and a little water until smooth (2 min). Strain through a sieve. Boil the liquid, stirring, 8–10 min until it thickens slightly. Sweeten with sugar, cool, and refrigerate. Serve cold.
Masa: Mix rice flour with a pinch of yeast, sugar, and enough water for a thick batter (2 min). Let rest 30 min. The batter should be pourable but not runny.
Heat a greased pan or traditional masa mold over medium heat. Pour small rounds of batter; cook 2–3 min until bubbles form and edges set, then flip and cook 1–2 min until golden. Repeat in batches.
Serve masa warm with honey or sugar syrup; drink kunu on the side for a traditional Hausa suhoor.

suhoor.name: Bangladeshi Panta Bhat
suhoor.description: Fermented rice soaked in water, served with chili and salt
suhoor.benefits: Cooling and hydrating; traditional Bengali suhoor
suhoor.tips: Often eaten with fried fish or bhorta (mashed vegetables)
steps: The night before: cook plain white rice (slightly more water than usual so it’s soft). Let cool completely, then transfer to a bowl, cover with water, and leave at room temperature overnight to ferment lightly.
In the morning: the rice will be slightly sour and swollen. Drain off some water if you prefer thicker, or add cold water to thin. Add a good pinch of salt and mix (1 min).
Serve in a bowl with sliced raw onion, green chili, and a drizzle of mustard oil if you have it (2 min). Optional: serve with fried fish, bhorta (mashed potato or eggplant), or lime.
Eat with your hands or a spoon; it’s cooling and hydrating for suhoor.

suhoor.name: Kenyan Mandazi & Chai
suhoor.description: Sweet fried dough (mandazi) with spiced chai tea
suhoor.benefits: Quick energy from carbs; chai helps with warmth and alertness
suhoor.tips: Common Swahili coast suhoor; pair with dates or fruit
steps: Mandazi: Mix 2 cups flour, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp baking powder, a pinch of salt, and 1/4 tsp cardamom. Add about 1/2 cup milk and 1 tbsp oil; knead into a soft dough (5 min). Rest 15 min.
Roll dough 1/2 in thick. Cut into triangles or circles. Heat oil in a deep pan; fry mandazi in batches 2–3 min per side until puffed and golden. Drain on paper towels.
Chai: Boil water with crushed ginger and cardamom pods (or powder) 2 min. Add black tea leaves and simmer 2 min. Add milk and sugar; bring to a gentle boil 1–2 min. Strain and serve hot.
Serve mandazi with chai and optional dates or fruit for a quick suhoor.

suhoor.name: Bosnian Burek
suhoor.description: Flaky pastry filled with meat, cheese, or spinach
suhoor.benefits: Filling and protein-rich; traditional Balkan pre-dawn meal
suhoor.tips: Often eaten with yogurt; popular in Sarajevo for suhoor
steps: Filling: Sauté finely chopped onion 3–4 min; add ground beef or lamb and cook 8–10 min until no pink remains. Season with salt, pepper, and a little paprika. Cool. (For cheese: mix feta with an egg; for spinach: sauté spinach with onion 5 min, drain, mix with cheese and egg.)

Thaw phyllo if frozen. Keep covered with a damp towel. Brush a baking dish with melted butter. Layer 2–3 sheets of phyllo, brushing each with butter; spread a thin layer of filling. Repeat layers until filling is used, ending with phyllo. Brush top with butter (about 15 min).
Score the top into squares or diamonds. Bake at 375°F (190°C) 35–45 min until golden and crisp.
Let rest 10 min. Serve warm with plain yogurt on the side.

suhoor.name: Somali Canjeero
suhoor.description: Soft fermented pancake with honey and ghee, often with liver or eggs
suhoor.benefits: Light and digestible; traditional Somali suhoor before dawn
suhoor.tips: Canjeero (lahoh) is a staple across Somalia and Djibouti; serve with honey and tea
steps: The night before: mix 2 cups sorghum or rice flour with 1/2 tsp yeast, 1 tsp sugar, and 2 cups warm water. Whisk until smooth; cover and leave 8–12 hours to ferment.
In the morning: batter should be bubbly. Heat a nonstick pan over medium; pour a ladle of batter in a spiral from the center. Do not spread. Cover 2–3 min until set and holes form on top.
Cook uncovered 1 min; no need to flip. Remove and keep warm. Repeat with remaining batter.
Serve canjeero with ghee, honey, and optional scrambled eggs or liver for a filling suhoor.

iftar.name: Traditional Date & Water Start
iftar.description: The Prophetic way to break fast - dates and water first
iftar.benefits: Natural sugars provide quick energy; dates are easily digestible
iftar.tips: Eat 1-3 dates and drink water, then pray Maghrib before the main meal
iftar.significance: The Prophet (peace be upon him) broke his fast with dates and water; this tradition is followed by Muslims worldwide at iftar.
steps: At Maghrib (sunset), break your fast with 1–3 dates (Medjool or any variety).
Drink a glass of water. Optionally drink a little milk.
Pray Maghrib, then proceed to your main iftar meal.

iftar.name: Moroccan Harira Soup
iftar.description: Hearty tomato-based soup with lentils, chickpeas, and fresh herbs
iftar.benefits: Rehydrating, protein-rich, and gentle on the stomach after fasting
iftar.tips: Serve with chebakia (honey cookies) for a traditional experience
iftar.significance: Harira is the iconic iftar soup in Morocco, often served with dates and chebakia during Ramadan.

sources.title: UNESCO – Iftar and its socio-cultural traditions

steps: Sauté 2 stalks chopped celery, 1 large chopped onion, and 1 tbsp grated ginger in 2 tbsp olive oil 5–6 min until soft. Add 4–5 chopped tomatoes (or 1 can) and cook 5–7 min until broken down.

Add 1/2 cup red lentils, 1 cup cooked chickpeas, 6 cups water or broth, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp pepper, and 1 tbsp tomato paste. Bring to a boil (2 min), then simmer 25–30 min until lentils are tender.
Stir in 1/2 cup chopped cilantro and 1–2 tbsp lemon juice. Add 1–2 tbsp flour or tadouira (flour-water paste) to thicken if desired. Adjust salt to taste (1 min).
Serve hot with dates and chebakia (honey sesame cookies) on the side for a traditional Moroccan iftar.

iftar.name: Pakistani Fruit Chaat
iftar.description: Refreshing mixed fruit salad with chaat masala and lime
iftar.benefits: Hydrating fruits with electrolytes and vitamins
iftar.tips: Use a variety of colorful fruits for maximum nutrition
steps: Wash and dry seasonal fruits: 1 apple, 1–2 bananas, 1 mango, 1/2 papaya, 1 cup grapes, 1/2 cup pomegranate seeds, 1 orange (segmented), 1 cup melon cubes (2 min). Cut into bite-sized pieces (5 min).
Combine all fruit in a large bowl. Squeeze juice of 1–2 limes over the fruit and toss gently (1 min).
Sprinkle 1–2 tsp chaat masala and a pinch of black salt (kala namak) if you have it. Add 2 tbsp chopped fresh mint and 1 tsp sugar or honey if fruit is tart (1 min).
Chill 5–10 min or serve at room temperature. Garnish with extra mint. Perfect to break fast and rehydrate.

iftar.name: Egyptian Konafa
iftar.description: Sweet cheese pastry with crispy kadaif and sugar syrup
iftar.tips: Balance sweet treats with protein-rich main dishes
steps: Thaw 1 lb (450g) kadaif (shredded phyllo) if frozen (about 30 min). Separate strands gently, mix with 1/2 cup melted butter until evenly coated (2 min). Press half into a greased 9x13 inch baking dish.
Layer 12–14 oz (350–400g) akkawi or mild white cheese (rinsed if salty) over the kadaif. Top with the remaining kadaif and press gently to seal (2 min).
Bake in a preheated 350°F (180°C) oven 25–30 min until golden and crisp on top.

Meanwhile, make sugar syrup: boil 2 cups sugar, 1 cup water, 1 tbsp lemon juice, and 1 tsp rose water 5–7 min until slightly thickened; cool 10 min. Pour syrup over hot konafa as soon as it comes out of the oven. Let absorb 10–15 min before serving. Garnish with pistachios if desired.

iftar.name: Arabian Chicken Mandi
iftar.description: Aromatic spiced rice with tender chicken, cooked in traditional style
iftar.benefits: Complete meal with proteins and carbohydrates for recovery
iftar.tips: Serve with raita and fresh salad for balance
steps: Marinate whole chicken or pieces with mandi spice (baharat, turmeric, cumin, coriander, cardamom, black pepper), salt, oil, and grated onion (5 min). Let sit 30 min.
In a large pot, sauté sliced onions 5–6 min until golden. Add mandi spice, dried lime (black lime), and water or broth. Add chicken and simmer 45 min until tender. Remove chicken; reserve broth.
Soak basmati rice 20 min; drain. In the same pot, layer rice over the broth (add more water if needed). Place chicken on top. Cover and cook on low 25 min until rice is done and liquid is absorbed.
Optional: brown the chicken under the broiler 5–8 min. Serve rice and chicken on a platter with raita, salad, and lime.

iftar.name: Lebanese Fattoush & Jallab
iftar.description: Toasted bread salad with sumac and refreshing jallab (date and grape drink)
iftar.benefits: Hydrating salad and sweet drink; jallab is a Ramadan staple in Lebanon
iftar.tips: Jallab is often served with ice and pine nuts; break fast with dates first
steps: Fattoush: Chop cucumber, tomatoes, radish, lettuce, and scallions into a bowl (5 min). Add chopped mint and parsley. Toss with sumac, a little salt, and olive oil (1 min).
Toast or fry pita 2–3 min until crisp; break into pieces. Add pita to the salad just before serving. Dress with pomegranate molasses and lemon juice; taste and adjust salt (1 min).
Jallab: Dissolve jallab syrup (grape molasses, date syrup, rose water) in cold water (1 min). Serve over ice; top with pine nuts and optional raisins.
Serve fattoush with jallab for a refreshing iftar start after dates and water.

iftar.name: Jordanian Mansaf
iftar.description: Lamb cooked in jameed (dried yogurt) sauce over rice, served on large platters
iftar.benefits: Jordan's national dish; protein and carbs for recovery after fasting
iftar.tips: Eaten communally at Ramadan gatherings; symbolizes hospitality
iftar.significance: Mansaf is central to Jordanian identity and is often served at special Ramadan and Eid gatherings.
steps: Soak jameed (dried yogurt balls) in warm water 2–3 hours; blend or mash until smooth (5 min). If using jameed paste, dilute with water.

In a large pot, brown lamb pieces in ghee or butter 5–7 min. Add water, bay leaf, and onion; simmer 1–1½ hours until lamb is tender. Add the jameed mixture and cook on low 20–30 min until the sauce thickens. Season with salt and a little allspice.
Cook long-grain rice (basmati or jasmine) in lamb broth or water 18–20 min until fluffy. Spread shrak or flatbread on a large platter; top with rice, then the lamb and jameed sauce (5 min).
Garnish with toasted pine nuts (2 min) and chopped parsley. Serve with more bread; eat with the right hand for a traditional experience.

iftar.name: Indonesian Kolak
iftar.description: Sweet coconut milk dessert with banana, sweet potato, and palm sugar
iftar.benefits: Quick energy and hydration; popular takjil (iftar snack) in Indonesia
iftar.tips: Kolak is one of the most common iftar sweets during Ramadan in Indonesia
steps: Peel and cube sweet potato (3 min); boil in water 10 min until tender. Drain and set aside.
In a pot, combine coconut milk, water, palm sugar (or brown sugar), a pinch of salt, and a knotted pandan leaf. Heat gently 3–4 min until sugar dissolves; do not boil hard.
Add the cooked sweet potato and sliced banana (use firm bananas). Simmer 5–8 min until banana is soft but not mushy.
Remove pandan leaf. Serve kolak warm or chilled as a takjil to break fast.

iftar.name: Nigerian Jollof Rice
iftar.description: One-pot spiced tomato rice with chicken or fish
iftar.benefits: Complete meal; festive dish at Nigerian Ramadan iftars
iftar.tips: Jollof is a centerpiece at West African iftar gatherings
steps: Blend tomatoes, onion, bell pepper, and Scotch bonnet (or habanero) into a smooth paste (2 min). Set aside.

In a large pot, heat oil; sauté sliced onion 5–6 min until golden. Add tomato paste and fry 2 min. Pour in the blended mix; cook 15–20 min until thick and oil rises. Add thyme, curry, bay leaf, salt, and stock cubes.

Add chicken pieces (or fish) and a little water; simmer 15 min. Add rinsed long-grain rice and enough broth or water to cover. Cover and cook on low 25 min until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork (1 min). Optional: add a layer of foil under the lid for a slight burn (party jollof). Serve with fried plantain or coleslaw.

iftar.name: Bangladeshi Piaju & Halim
iftar.description: Lentil fritters (piaju) and slow-cooked meat and lentil stew (halim)
iftar.totalTime: 200 min (+ overnight soak for halim, 2–3 hr for piaju dal)
iftar.benefits: Protein-rich and warming; halim is a Ramadan staple in Dhaka
iftar.tips: Piaju is a popular street iftar snack; halim is often sold in Chawk Bazaar
steps: Piaju: Soak yellow lentils (moong dal) 2–3 hours; drain and blend with sliced onion, green chili, salt, turmeric, and a little water to a coarse batter (3 min). Heat oil; drop spoonfuls of batter and fry 2–3 min per side until golden and crisp. Drain and serve with cilantro and lime.

Halim: Soak wheat berries and lentils (masoor/mung) overnight. In a large pot, brown beef or mutton with ginger-garlic paste and onions 8–10 min. Add drained wheat and lentils, enough water, and spices (turmeric, cumin, garam masala). Simmer 2–3 hours, stirring every 20–30 min, until thick and creamy.
Shred the meat in the pot (2 min). Adjust salt and spice. Serve halim hot, garnished with fried onion (3 min), ginger, cilantro, lime, and green chili.
Serve piaju as an iftar snack and halim as a main with bread or rice.

iftar.name: Bosnian Begova Čorba
iftar.description: Chicken and vegetable soup with okra and sour cream
iftar.benefits: Warming and rehydrating; traditional Bosnian iftar starter
iftar.tips: Served with bread; often the first dish at Sarajevo iftar tables
steps: In a large pot, simmer a whole chicken or pieces with onion, carrot, and celery 45 min until the meat is tender. Remove chicken; shred the meat and set aside (5 min). Strain the broth and return to the pot.
Add diced carrots and celery to the broth; simmer 8–10 min until tender. Add okra (fresh or frozen) and vermicelli; cook 8–10 min until okra is soft and noodles are done.

In a bowl, whisk an egg with a few spoonfuls of hot broth; stir in sour cream (1 min). Pour this mixture into the soup and stir on very low heat 2–3 min—do not boil. Add shredded chicken and season with salt, pepper, and a little lemon juice.
Serve hot with crusty bread and optional chopped parsley.

iftar.name: Kenyan Pilau
iftar.description: Spiced rice with meat, often served at communal iftars
iftar.benefits: Filling and aromatic; reflects Swahili and South Asian influences
iftar.tips: Common at Nairobi and Mombasa iftars; serve with kachumbari (tomato salad)
steps: Make pilau masala: toast and grind cumin, coriander, black pepper, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon 3–4 min (or use store-bought pilau masala).
In a large pot, heat oil; fry sliced onions 8–10 min until deeply golden. Add ginger-garlic paste, pilau masala, and tomato paste; fry 2 min. Add beef or chicken pieces and brown 5–7 min.

Add rinsed basmati rice, coconut milk, and enough water (about 1:1.5 rice to liquid). Add whole potatoes if you like. Bring to a boil (2 min), then cover and cook on low 25 min until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork (1 min). Serve with kachumbari (diced tomato, onion, cilantro, lime) and optional chutney.

iftar.name: Algerian Chorba
iftar.description: Hearty Ramadan soup with lamb, chickpeas, and vermicelli
iftar.benefits: Rehydrating and protein-rich; traditional Algerian iftar starter
iftar.tips: Chorba is the centerpiece of Algerian Ramadan; serve with dates and bourek
steps: In a large pot, brown 1 lb (450g) lamb pieces in 2 tbsp oil 5–7 min. Add 1 chopped onion, 2 cloves minced garlic; sauté 3 min. Add 4 chopped tomatoes, 1 tbsp tomato paste; cook 5 min.
Add 1 cup soaked or canned chickpeas, 2 tsp ras el hanout (or cumin, coriander, cinnamon), 1/2 tsp turmeric, 6 cups water or broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer 45 min until lamb is tender.
Add 1/2 cup broken vermicelli; cook 5–7 min until soft. Stir in 1/2 cup chopped cilantro and 2 tbsp lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper (1 min).
Serve hot with dates and bread. Optional: add a dollop of harissa for heat.

iftar.name: Tunisian Lablabi
iftar.description: Spiced chickpea soup with bread, egg, and harissa
iftar.benefits: Quick, filling, and hydrating; classic Tunisian iftar
iftar.tips: Lablabi is often eaten from a communal bowl; add stale bread to thicken
steps: In a pot, heat 2 cups cooked chickpeas (canned) with 3–4 cups broth or water. Add 2 tsp cumin, 3 cloves minced garlic, 1 tbsp harissa, and salt. Simmer 15 min.
Toast or fry 2–3 slices stale bread 2–3 min until crisp. Place in bowls. Poach or soft-boil 1–2 eggs per person (3–4 min for soft).
Ladle hot chickpea soup over the bread. Top with a poached egg, drizzle of olive oil, more cumin, and harissa. Add capers and tuna if you like (optional).
Serve immediately with lemon wedges. Eat with a spoon, mixing bread and soup.

iftar.name: Senegalese Thieboudienne
iftar.description: Rice with fish, vegetables, and tomato sauce - Senegal's national dish
iftar.benefits: Complete meal with protein and vegetables; central to Senegalese Ramadan
iftar.tips: Thieb (ceebu jën) is served at ndogou (breaking fast); use firm white fish

sources.title: UNESCO – Iftar and its socio-cultural traditions

steps: Season 2 lbs (900g) fish (tilapia, grouper, or sea bass) with salt, pepper, and 1 tbsp mustard. Heat 1/4 cup oil in a large pot; fry fish 4–5 min per side. Set aside.

In same pot, sauté 2 chopped onions 5 min. Add 3 tbsp tomato paste, 2 chopped tomatoes, 1 tbsp fish paste (optional), 1 tsp garlic. Cook 10 min. Add 1/2 head cabbage (quartered), 3 carrots, 1 eggplant (chunks), 2 cups water. Simmer 20 min.
Add 2 cups broken rice (or regular rice), more water to cover, and fish on top. Cover and cook 25 min until rice is tender. Add water if needed.
Serve on a large platter: rice first, then vegetables and fish. Drizzle with remaining sauce. Eat communally for ndogou (breaking fast).

iftar.name: Malaysian Bubur Lambuk
iftar.description: Savory rice porridge with beef, coconut milk, and spices - mosque charity iftar staple
iftar.benefits: Rehydrating and nourishing; shared at mosque iftars across Malaysia
iftar.tips: Bubur lambuk is traditionally prepared by mosque communities and distributed at iftar
steps: Rinse 1 cup rice and soak 15 min; drain. In a large pot, sauté 2 tbsp grated ginger, 2 cinnamon sticks, 2 star anise in 1 tbsp oil 2 min. Add 1 lb (450g) cubed beef; brown 5 min.
Add rice, 6 cups water, and 1 cup coconut milk. Bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer 45–60 min, stirring often, until rice breaks down and beef is tender.
Season with salt, white pepper, and a little sugar. Add more water if too thick. Stir in 1/2 cup coconut milk (2 min).
Serve hot in bowls topped with fried shallots, sliced scallions, and optional sambal. Often shared as communal iftar at mosques.

iftar.name: Iranian Ash Reshteh
iftar.description: Hearty noodle and bean soup with herbs, kashk, and fried mint
iftar.benefits: Protein-rich and warming; traditional Persian iftar and Nowruz dish
iftar.tips: Kashk (whey) gives a tangy finish; find it at Middle Eastern grocers or omit
steps: Soak 1/2 cup chickpeas and 1/2 cup lentils 30 min (or use canned). In a large pot, sauté 2 chopped onions 5 min. Add 8 cups water, chickpeas, lentils; simmer 30 min.
Add 2 cups chopped spinach, 1 cup chopped parsley, 1 cup chopped cilantro, 1 cup chopped scallions. Cook 15 min. Add 2 cups reshteh (Persian noodles) or linguine broken in half; cook 10 min.
Stir in 2 tbsp dried mint, 1 tsp turmeric, salt, and pepper. Thin 2–3 tbsp kashk with a little soup; stir in (or omit). Simmer 5 min.
Serve in bowls; drizzle with kashk and fried mint (mint + oil). Garnish with fried onion. Common at Iranian iftar tables.

iftar.name: Palestinian Musakhan
iftar.description: Sumac-roasted chicken on taboon bread with caramelized onions and pine nuts
iftar.benefits: Celebration dish; sumac and olive oil are staples of Palestinian cuisine
iftar.tips: Musakhan is often served at Ramadan and family gatherings; eat with hands
steps: Marinate chicken pieces with 3 tbsp sumac, 1 tsp allspice, salt, pepper, and 2 tbsp olive oil (5 min). Caramelize 4 sliced onions in 1/4 cup olive oil 15–20 min; add 2 tbsp sumac (2 min).
Roast chicken at 400°F (200°C) 40–45 min until golden. Warm taboon or large pita in the oven (2 min). Toast pine nuts in a dry pan 2–3 min.
Place bread on a platter. Top with onion mixture, then chicken. Drizzle with pan juices and olive oil; scatter pine nuts and more sumac.
Serve with yogurt and salad. A centerpiece at Palestinian iftar.

iftar.name: Indian Chana Chaat
iftar.description: Spiced chickpea salad with chaat masala, lime, and fresh herbs
iftar.benefits: Quick, hydrating, and protein-rich; popular iftar snack across India and Pakistan
iftar.tips: Use canned chickpeas for speed; chaat masala is available at South Asian grocers
steps: Drain and rinse 2 cans chickpeas; put in a large bowl. Dice 2 tomatoes, 1 red onion; add to bowl (3 min).
Add 2 tsp chaat masala, 1/2 tsp cumin, pinch black salt (kala namak) if you have it, salt to taste. Squeeze juice of 2 limes; toss (2 min).
Add 1/2 cup chopped cilantro and 2 tbsp chopped mint. Add a handful of sev (crispy noodles) or crushed papdi just before serving (1 min).
Serve at room temperature or chilled. A refreshing start to iftar.
